protocol.dispatcher: relay only: never codes, never triages, never writes backlog notes, never passes uncited claims; only escalates or transitions tasks
protocol.loop: architect (only if task not ref'd in SPEC) -> implement -> review -> architect-decision (only on unknown/scoping questions or >1 critical review finding) -> merge + deploy
protocol.worktrees: ALL code changes in worktrees under .worktrees/ (repo convention); every dispatch ends merged or returned with named blocker
protocol.notes: agents append output to the task's backlog notes; dispatcher pulls notes from the task to determine next steps; dispatcher never writes notes
protocol.blindReview: CORRECTED DEFINITION (user challenge 2026-08-12): review dispatch contains ONLY item identifier + work-order pointer (e.g. SPEC §) + worktree path. Reviewer reads the item BODY and the CODE; explicitly FORBIDDEN from reading the implementer appended notes; dispatcher NEVER relays implementer claims into the review prompt (no special asks, no priming). Deviations/claims judged by the reviewer from the code alone or not at all. VIOLATED on BUG-018/BUG-019/BUG-021/DEBT-031 reviews (implementer claims relayed in prose) — acknowledged, corrected from here.
protocol.reviewRules: every review note must be fixed; >1 critical issue -> architect-decision reviews scoping (rearchitect vs implement, which agent, how to split)
protocol.backlog: dispatcher may only escalate or transition tasks; transitions carry citations (required for terminal statuses); item status changes via backlog CLI/MCP only; BL-225 red→green gate on any resolve
protocol.verification: outcomes verified from state-side evidence (git refs, test output, backlog notes) — never executor prose; live-status + upstream-consumer verification after any deploy
protocol.perItemCycle: CODE-FIRST TWO-LOOP (user directive 2026-08-12, supersedes test-first): LOOP1 code-until-clean: implement = code only + direct build/lint/typecheck on affected (NO test authoring/runs) -> code review = reviewer reads ONLY code, no test runs -> fix notes -> repeat until clean. LOOP2 tests-after-clean: implement = author tests on clean code + lint/typecheck + targeted test runs (BL-225 red-to-green shown via fix toggle: RED off + GREEN on) -> code review = reviewer reviews tests AND RUNS tests AND diagnoses test-vs-code issues -> fix notes -> repeat until complete. THEN merge + ONE consolidated verification (full affected suites + tree-state quotes + smoke). Applies from DEBT-004 (T8) onward.
protocol.claims: CLAIM-PER-DISPATCH (user directive 2026-08-12): every dispatched agent CLAIMS the backlog item at dispatch start via backlog claim-item --by <agent>:<instance>, renews on long runs (30-min staleness), releases unconditionally on every exit path. Claim timestamps = measured phase starts (implement start = claim). T1-T5 have ZERO claim events (protocol gap — dispatch times unlogged, est only); applies from remaining T7 legs + T6.2 + T8-T11 onward.

executionNotes: REVERT RULE (user directive 2026-08-12): if changes on main are reverted for any reason, REBUILD ALL AFFECTED artifacts afterward — nx build for every affected project (store-adapter, graph-store, and any consumer bundles that embed them, incl. memory-bundle members), then `npx nx run registry:sync-index` + commit the regenerated registry/index.json with sources, then smoke test (`rm -rf dist/smoke && node scripts/smoke-test.mjs` -> summary.failed===0), then verify live consumers (memory-server etc.). A source-only revert leaves stale dists carrying the reverted code — the exact hazard BUG-014/DEBT-003 fight. Reverts themselves: agent-dispatched via git revert/restore of specific paths only (no reset --hard, no stash), never by the dispatcher.
